subject: cs-9
description: Entrepreneurial mindset, business planning, market survey, design thinking, prototyping, digital marketing, pitching, and freelancing.

questions.question: An entrepreneur is best described as:

options.A: A government employee managing public funds
options.B: A person who starts and manages a business taking financial risks for profit
options.C: A scientist who invents new technologies
options.D: An employee working in a large corporation

questions.explanation: an entrepreneur 'starts or owns a business, organizes and manages it taking on financial risks for the sake of profit'.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a successful entrepreneur?

options.B: Taking wild, uncalculated risks
options.D: Depending entirely on others for decisions

questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs are not wild risk takers but are instead calculated risk takers. — listing this as 'Preference for moderate risk'.

questions.question: The process of creating an enterprise is called:

options.B: Entrepreneurship

questions.explanation: The process of creating an enterprise is called entrepreneurship.. It involves calculating risks with confidence to achieve predetermined business or industrial objectives.

questions.question: An entrepreneur shifts economic resources from areas of lower productivity to:

options.B: Areas of higher productivity and greater yield

questions.explanation: the entrepreneur is 'he who shifts economic resources out of an area of lower and into the area of higher productivity and greater yield'.

questions.question: 'Desire for responsibility' as an entrepreneurial characteristic means:

options.A: Delegating all important tasks to employees
options.B: Feeling a deep sense of personal responsibility for venture outcomes and preferring control of resources
options.D: Relying on investors to take responsibility

questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs feel a deep sense of personal responsibility for the outcome of ventures they start. They prefer to be in control of their resources.

questions.question: Self-reliance in entrepreneurship means:

options.A: Hiring as many employees as possible from the start
options.B: Performing many roles themselves especially in early days, not shying away from responsibility
options.C: Relying on investors to make all decisions
options.D: Avoiding difficult tasks and delegating everything

questions.explanation: self-reliant entrepreneurs 'end up performing many jobs themselves, even those they know little about' and 'do not shy away from the responsibility for making their businesses succeed'.

questions.question: 'Confidence in their ability to succeed' explains why some entrepreneurs:

options.A: Give up quickly when they face their first failure
options.B: Have failed in business — often more than once — before finally succeeding
options.D: Always choose safe and proven business models

questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs. high levels of optimism may explain why some of the most successful entrepreneurs have failed in business — often more than once — before finally succeeding.'

questions.question: The characteristic 'Determination' is also described in as:

options.B: Grit — the ability to focus intently on achieving a singular long-term goal
options.C: Being stubborn about refusing to change plans
options.D: Managing employees with a firm hand

questions.explanation: The ability to focus intently on achieving a singular, long-term goal. Studies show that grit is a reliable predictor of achievement and success.

questions.question: 'Future orientation' as an entrepreneurial characteristic means:

options.A: Planning only for the next week
options.B: Looking ahead and focusing more on what they might do tomorrow than on past achievements
options.C: Focusing on what competitors did in the past
options.D: Managing the current financial situation only

questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs have a well-defined sense of searching for opportunities. They look ahead and are less concerned with what they did yesterday than with what they might do tomorrow.

questions.question: 'Skill at organizing' in entrepreneurship means:

options.A: Keeping paperwork neat and filing documents properly
options.B: Knowing how to put the right people together to accomplish a task and transform visions into reality

questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs know how to put the right people together to accomplish a task. Effectively combining people and jobs enables entrepreneurs to transform their visions into reality.

questions.question: One common misconception about entrepreneurs is that:

options.B: They are driven wholly by the desire to make money, when in fact achievement is their primary motivating force

questions.explanation: One of the most common misconceptions about entrepreneurs is that they are driven wholly by the desire to make money. To the contrary, achievement seems to be their primary motivating force; money is simply a way of keeping score.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a BENEFIT of entrepreneurship in ?

options.B: Job security similar to government work
options.C: Gaining control over your life, becoming self-fulfilled, and reaping unlimited profits

questions.explanation: benefits as: 'gain control over their lives, make a difference in the world, become self-fulfilled, reap unlimited profits, contribute to society, and do what they enjoy doing.'

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a DRAWBACK of entrepreneurship in ?

options.B: Making a difference in the world
options.C: Uncertainty of income, risk of losing investments, long hours, high stress, and complete decision-making responsibility

questions.explanation: drawbacks as: 'uncertainty of income, the risk of losing their investments, long hours and hard work, a lower quality of life until the business gets established, high stress levels, and complete decision-making responsibility.'

questions.question: Entrepreneurs 'see potential where most people see only':.

options.B: Problems or nothing at all — a characteristic that makes them objects of ridicule until their ideas succeed

questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs see potential where most people see only problems or nothing at all, a characteristic that often makes them the objects of ridicule (at least until their ideas become huge successes). Topic 7.1.3 — Design Thinking

questions.question: Design Thinking is a problem-solving process that is:

options.B: Iterative and human-centered

questions.explanation: Design Thinking is iterative (repeating stages) and human-centered (focused on user needs). Stages can be revisited and repeated as needed.

questions.question: The correct order of the Design Thinking phases is:

options.B: Empathize → Define → Ideate → Prototype → Test

questions.explanation: Design Thinking follows: Empathize (understand users), Define (state the problem), Ideate (brainstorm), Prototype (build), Test (evaluate).

questions.question: The 'Ideate' phase of Design Thinking focuses on:

options.B: Building a physical model
options.C: Brainstorming a wide range of creative solutions

questions.explanation: Ideation involves generating as many creative ideas as possible without judgment — quantity over quality is encouraged at this stage.

questions.question: Design Thinking has how many phases?
questions.explanation: Design Thinking 'contains five phases: 1. Empathize, 2. Define, 3. Ideate, 4. Prototype and 5. Test'.

questions.question: The 'Empathize' phase of Design Thinking involves:

options.A: Building a model of the solution
options.B: Brainstorming creative ideas
options.C: Understanding users' needs and challenges through observation and interviews

questions.explanation: the Empathize phase involves 'understanding users' needs and challenges through observation and interviews'.

questions.question: The 'Define' phase of Design Thinking involves:

options.A: Generating as many ideas as possible
options.B: Building a prototype for testing
options.C: Defining the problem clearly based on insights gathered from Empathize
options.D: Testing the final product with real users

questions.explanation: Define involves 'defining the problem based on the insights gathered' from the Empathize phase.

questions.question: The 'Prototype' phase of Design Thinking involves:

options.B: Brainstorming solutions without restrictions
options.C: Turning the most promising ideas into simple models for testing
options.D: Testing models with real users for feedback

questions.explanation: Prototype — the most promising ideas are turned into simple prototypes for testing..

questions.question: The 'Test' phase of Design Thinking involves:

options.B: Building the first physical model
options.D: Testing prototypes with real users to gather feedback and refine the design

questions.explanation: Test — these prototypes are tested with real users to gather feedback and refine the design..

questions.question: Design Thinking is described as 'non-linear' because:

options.A: It does not involve any structured steps
options.B: Stages can be carried out in parallel, repeated, and revisited at any point in the process
options.C: It skips directly to the testing phase
options.D: It can only be applied to design, not business problems

questions.explanation: One can carry these stages out in parallel, repeat them and circle back to a previous stage at any point in the process.

questions.question: Which global brands are mentioned in as having rapidly adopted Design Thinking?

options.B: Apple, Google and Samsung

questions.explanation: Some of the world.s leading brands, such as Apple, Google and Samsung, rapidly adopted the design thinking approach.'

questions.question: Which Pakistani institutions are mentioned in as implementing Design Thinking?

options.B: Punjab University and Karachi University
options.C: IBA Karachi, NUST, NED, COMSATS and Pak-Austria Fachhochschule

questions.explanation: Design Thinking is 'also implemented in Pakistan like IBA Karachi, NUST, NED, COMSATS and Pak-Austria Fachhochschule etc.'

questions.question: Which global universities are mentioned in as teaching Design Thinking?

options.B: Stanford, Harvard, Imperial College London

questions.explanation: leading universities around the world teach the related methodology — including Stanford, Harvard, Imperial College London etc. Topics 7.1.4 to 7.3 — Business Plan, Market Analysis, Pricing & Financial Planning

questions.question: A business plan is MOST important for:

options.B: Guiding the entrepreneur and attracting financing for the startup
options.C: Hiring employees after the business launches
options.D: Paying taxes after profits are made

questions.explanation: The primary goals of the business plan are to guide entrepreneurs as they launch their businesses and to help them acquire the necessary financing to launch.

questions.question: What does the 'M' in SMART goals stand for?

options.B: Measurable

questions.explanation: SMART stands for: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, and Time-bound. Measurable means goals must be quantifiable and assessable.

questions.question: The executive summary in a business plan should be written:

options.A: First, as an introduction to the plan
options.B: Last, after the entire business plan is completed

questions.explanation: Once you have developed the whole business plan only then in the end an executive summary is devised; like a cherry on the top.

questions.question: SWOT analysis examines:

options.B: Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats

questions.explanation: SWOT analyzes internal factors (Strengths, Weaknesses) and external factors (Opportunities, Threats) affecting a business or product.

questions.question: The formula for calculating SELLING PRICE is:

options.B: Cost of Production + Overheads + Profit

questions.explanation: formula: Selling Price = Cost of Production + Overheads + Profit. All three components must be calculated accurately.

questions.question: If demand for a product is HIGH and supply is LOW, the price should:

options.B: Decrease significantly

questions.explanation: If demand is great for the available supply, the price (and thus the profit) may be increased. When supply exceeds demand, prices drop.

questions.question: Which of the following is a DRAWBACK of entrepreneurship?

options.B: Potentially unlimited profits
options.C: Uncertainty of income and high stress levels
options.D: Making a difference in your community

questions.explanation: Entrepreneurship comes with financial uncertainty, risk of failure, long hours, high stress, and complete decision-making responsibility.

questions.question: A business plan is described in as the entrepreneur's:

options.B: Road map on the journey toward building a successful business

questions.explanation: The plan serves as an entrepreneur.s road map on the journey toward building a successful business.'

questions.question: What does SMART stand for in the context of entrepreneurial goals?

options.B: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, Time-Bound

questions.explanation: S-Specific (precise and clear), M-Measurable (quantifiable), A-Achievable (attainable), R-Realistic (grounded), T-Time-Bound (with a deadline).

questions.question: Which business plan software is described in as pre-loaded with more than 500 templates?

options.B: PlanWrite

questions.explanation: Business Plan Pro is LivePlan ideal for entrepreneurs writing their first business plan. This software comes pre-loaded with more than 500 business plan templates.

questions.question: Canva is described in as:

options.A: A paid spreadsheet program for budgets
options.B: A free online versatile app for creating graphics, videos and social media content

questions.explanation: Canva is a free to use online versatile app that lets you create stunning graphics, videos and social media content with ease.

questions.question: WordPress is described in as:

options.B: The leading website creation tool worldwide, powering over half of web content

questions.explanation: WordPress is the leading website creation tool worldwide, powering over half of the content. This open-source CMS is versatile and easy to use.

questions.question: 'Profit' is defined in as:

options.A: Total revenue earned in a year
options.B: The difference between the cost price and the selling price
options.C: The total amount of money invested

questions.explanation: Profit is the difference between the cost price and selling price. Part of this money can be put back into the business.

questions.question: When sales increase, what does say an entrepreneur can do with profit margins?

options.A: Always raise profit margins as sales grow
options.B: Keep profit margins fixed regardless of sales
options.C: Reduce profit margins to lower the selling price and expand the market

questions.explanation: When sales increase, profit margins may be reduced. This can enable the entrepreneur to lower the selling price, allowing the business to secure and even expand the market.

questions.question: 'Competitors' are defined in as:

options.B: Business people who provide similar products or services
options.C: Government agencies that regulate the market

questions.explanation: Business people who provide similar products or service are competitors.

questions.question: The COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) in 's candy-making example includes:

options.B: Raw materials, production labor, and packaging

questions.explanation: COGS 'includes all the direct costs related to producing the candy. It involves raw materials, production labor and packaging.'

questions.question: In the candy example, if 1 kg sugar costs Rs.150, 2 kg chocolate costs Rs.800, and flavoring costs Rs.75, what is the total raw material cost for one batch?
questions.explanation: calculation: Sugar Rs.150 + Chocolate Rs.800 + Flavoring Rs.75 = Rs.1025 total raw materials for one batch (making 20 units of candy).

questions.question: An entrepreneur identifies business ideas by:

options.A: Copying successful businesses from other countries
options.B: Considering community needs and determining what product or service could address those needs
options.C: Waiting for investors to suggest ideas
options.D: Only focusing on products they personally enjoy using

questions.explanation: An entrepreneur should consider their community and identify its needs for products or services — identifying a difficulty and determining what product or service could overcome it.

questions.question: executive summary should be written:

options.A: On the very first day of planning
options.B: Before the market analysis section
options.C: After the entire business plan is complete — 'like a cherry on the top'

questions.explanation: the phrase 'like a cherry on the top' — the executive summary is the last thing written but appears first in the document, condensing the entire plan.

questions.question: The 'Analyze the Market' section of a business plan uses which tool to evaluate advantages, disadvantages, opportunities and risks?

options.B: Flowchart

questions.explanation: SWOT analysis is a good technique to evaluate your product in context of the market. Your advantages, disadvantages, possibilities, and risks are examined in a SWOT analysis.

questions.question: A market survey for a business should answer which of the following questions?

options.A: How many employees do competitors have?
options.B: Who are the customers, why do they like the product, and are they willing to pay a commercial price?
options.C: What is the government tax rate on the product?
options.D: How much profit are similar businesses making?

questions.explanation: survey questions including: who are the people interested, why they like/dislike the product, whether they are willing to pay a commercial price, and whether demand is sustainable.
